Washington hosts Los Angeles tonight, and the model has it close: 3.10 expected goals for WSH against 2.92 for LAK. (Expected goals measure the quality of chances.) At five on five, LAK has taken 51% of the expected goals in its games and WSH 49%, so there isn't much between them. LAK allows fewer chances per 60 minutes (2.64 expected goals against, versus 3.85 for WSH), while WSH creates more (3.36 for, versus 2.69). On special teams, WSH's penalty kill gives up 0.99 expected goals a game, and the Capitals take 4.9 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays.

In net, projected starter Logan Thompson (WSH) is at +5.9 goals saved above expected this season, which compares his saves to what the shot quality would predict, after +28.16 last year. Projected LAK starter Darcy Kuemper is at -5.26 this season and -6.77 last year. Los Angeles is 0-3-2 in its last five, with 51% of the expected goals in those games, and the Kings are without Mats Zuccarello (injured reserve). Washington is 3-2-0 over its last five, and Pierre-Luc Dubois is out with illness.

The Kings' record looks worse than their play: they have been outscored 25-12 during a winless stretch, while the chances say it's mostly bad luck. Washington's results run ahead of its chances, with goaltending doing the lifting. For Los Angeles, Artemi Panarin has a 33% chance to score and a 71% chance to record a point, and the model calls him due. For Washington, Alex Tuch is the model's pick at 35% to score.
